status: Closed — explicit editor provenance is separated from actor/model identity across supported surfaces
finding: The active governed claim correctly records `Codex-GPT5.6 Terra`, while generic environment detection still reports legacy `codex-gpt-5.4-mini`; an operator cannot distinguish verified runtime model provenance from a user-authorized actor label. A second dogfood case showed the same defect for the active Codex editor surface: the actor identity should be `Codex-GPT 5.5` from the Codex editor plus the current model code, but `next` integration metadata still exposed stale `AGENT_IDENTITY=codex-gpt-5.4-mini`. This does not mean every agent should be called Codex, and it does not mean every suffix is an editor: for example `Fable 5` is a model code, not an editor surface.
expectedBehavior: Surface actor label, provider/model provenance, editor/surface id, and confidence/source separately. Never infer a model identity from a legacy editor environment variable. Actor identity should be assembled from the current editor/surface plus current model code when available: current supported editor surfaces are Codex, Claude, Antigravity, Cursor, and Copilot. Codex editor plus GPT 5.5 can produce `Codex-GPT 5.5`, while a Claude surface using Fable 5 should preserve Claude as the surface and Fable 5 as the model code. Stale environment aliases should be reported only as low-confidence legacy hints.
evidenceOrRepro: Confirmed while finishing TASK-TEAM-0074; the task ledger claim was Terra and `next` integration metadata exposed the stale environment value. Reconfirmed on 2026-07-14 while operating from the Codex editor as `Codex-GPT 5.5`: `node atm.mjs next --prompt ... --json` failed route selection but still reported `integrationBootstrap.currentEditorDetectedFrom: AGENT_IDENTITY` and `currentEditorRawValue: codex-gpt-5.4-mini`, prompting corrections that Codex is the editor surface for this session, the current editor set is Codex/Claude/Antigravity/Cursor/Copilot, and Fable 5 is a model code, not an editor. On 2026-09-05, `packages/cli/src/commands/integration/adapters.ts` was repaired so only explicit `ATM_EDITOR_ID` (or `CODEX_HOME` fallback) can establish editor provenance; `AGENT_IDENTITY` values including `codex-gpt-5.4-mini`, `claude-opus-5`, `cursor-captain`, and `Fable 5` now produce no editor. Focused regression, typecheck, adjacent next-contract tests, and the sealed runner publication passed in `3bbb3d7270d679a84c8299a41796d283cfadcf4f` / `d4d5490ad3bb11a834d768b3d185a27066054dfc`.
followUp: Keep the cross-surface provenance regressions in the CLI validation suite; stale `AGENT_IDENTITY` remains a low-confidence legacy hint and must not establish editor provenance.
